size.note: Wikipedia gives the male as 30 cm and the female as 34 cm, and says they otherwise look alike.

habitat: Marshes, savannah, grassland, bracken, undergrowth and clearings in woodland, occasionally reeds and papyrus. Usually below 1,500 m.
summary: In breeding plumage the head, body and tail are black, with some buff barring on the rump and rufous wings. Outside the breeding season the upper parts are dark brown with rufous barring. Juveniles are rufous with dark and light barring and streaking. Wikipedia says it is resident in some places and migrant in others, so no single status was stored. The page used does not describe the voice. The Kemp code VB was left unchanged.

similar.note: Burchell’s Coucal has white underparts. A breeding Black Coucal is black on the head, body and tail, with rufous wings.

population.notes: Kemp et al. 2001 order-of-magnitude threshold 2^3=8 mature individuals (visiting breeder); paper interval half–double → 4–16.

sources.title: Kemp A.C., Herholdt J.J., Whyte I. & Harrison J. (2001). Birds of the two largest national parks in South Africa: a method to generate estimates of population size for all species and assess their conservation ecology. S. Afr. J. Sci. 97: 393–403.

calls.description: The Wikipedia page used here does not describe the voice. Grade A song from Kamfinsa, Zambia. The filename names Black Coucal and the song. No grade A recording from South Africa or Kruger was in the catalogue set.
